title: Load and unload three boxes
summary: Count boxes with two counters to run a fixed batch: load three, unload three, then light Done.
scope: Tests give deterministic native POSIX host evidence on a simulated plant scene; they are not physical, hardware, HIL, or certification evidence.
objectives: Count items with a counter that has a preset value.
Use one counter to stop loading and another to know the batch is finished.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/CountedQueue.st, count the boxes at EyeIn with a CTU of preset 3 and the boxes at EyeOut with a second CTU of preset 3.
stages.checkpoint: Load one box at a time, stop loading at the third, and light Done when the second counter reaches 3.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, count the boxes: three are loaded, one after the other, and then the belt unloads them.
stages.checkpoint: The belt runs and boxes appear until three have passed EyeIn; Done stays off until the third box has passed EyeOut, and then the belt stops.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then run: The starter has no counters; load three boxes with a counter at EyeIn, count the unloaded boxes with a counter at EyeOut, light Done when all three are out, and stop the belt then.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: In Tests, choose the saved zplc.json and run only the counted-queue scenario; watch the 3D view while it runs.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named counted-queue and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the boxes enter one by one and leave at the other end; the counters change once per box, not once per scan.
stages.checkpoint: All three boxes are delivered, none is dropped or collides, and Done is on when the belt stops.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: A counter counts rising edges, so a box that stays under a sensor counts once; the final AT assertion pins Done and the stopped belt.
stages.checkpoint: It does not establish physical belt speed, sensor response, hardware timing, HIL, or certification.

hints.text: Declare two CTU instances and call each with CU wired to its sensor, R := FALSE and PV := 3; the Q output turns on when the count reaches the preset.
Emit a new box on Start and each time the previous box has left EyeIn (an F_TRIG on EyeIn), until the first counter is done; then Done := Unloaded.Q and Run := Active AND NOT Unloaded.Q.

faultCases: The starter has no counters; load three boxes with a counter at EyeIn, count the unloaded boxes with a counter at EyeOut, light Done when all three are out, and stop the belt then.
